query: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In CrMnFeCoNi high‐entropy alloys and related compositions with minor elemental tuning, the predictive approach accurately identifies materials with low phonon thermal conductivity by capturing the emergence of soft phonon modes induced by chemical disorder. These soft modes, whose energies are lowered due to local lattice distortions and force-constant fluctuations, play a decisive role in enhancing phonon scattering.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase CrMnFeCoNi and related high-entropy alloys with near-equiatomic compositions, exhibiting intrinsic chemical disorder.
generation.intervention: Perform in-situ high-resolution neutron scattering experiments, complemented by vibrational spectroscopy if needed, to measure detailed phonon dispersion relations with a focus on detecting and quantifying soft vibrational modes.
generation.conditions: Experiments conducted over a wide temperature range (10 K to 400 K) and under controlled pressure conditions, across several alloy compositions with slight elemental variations. Enhanced resolution and improved signal-to-noise settings are employed to unambiguously resolve the soft modes.
generation.structural_mediator: Soft vibrational modes and localized phonon states arising from chemically induced lattice distortions and force-constant fluctuations.
generation.mechanism: Chemical disorder in high-entropy alloys leads to local lattice distortions that soften specific phonon modes. This mode softening increases phonon scattering, which in turn reduces the lattice component of thermal conductivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: A strong quantitative correlation (approximately 80% or better) between the predicted and measured soft mode energies. Should the soft modes be detected within 10% of the predicted energy values, it would support the predictive model; significant deviations or failure to detect the modes would falsify the hypothesis.
generation.baseline: Conventional predictive models (e.g., Debye or perturbative approaches) that do not incorporate detailed chemical disorder effects, resulting in higher prediction errors for the lattice thermal conductivity.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is applicable to high-entropy alloys with near-equiatomic or slightly tuned compositions where chemical disorder is the dominant factor affecting phonon behavior. It may not hold in systems where microstructural factors (such as grain boundaries or secondary phase precipitates) predominate.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainties include the potential overlap of soft mode signals with other scattering phenomena and the challenge of isolating the effects of chemical disorder from other microstructural contributions. The exact quantitative improvement over existing models remains to be fully established.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform high-resolution, in-situ neutron scattering experiments on a series of CrMnFeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys under controlled temperature (10–400 K) and pressure conditions. Compare the measured phonon dispersion relations and soft mode energies directly with the predictions from the new model.
measurements: Detailed phonon dispersion curves across the Brillouin zone
Quantitative determination of soft phonon mode energies
Independent measurements of lattice thermal conductivity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured soft mode energies deviate by more than 10% from the predicted values or if the correlation between the soft mode characteristics and reduced thermal conductivity is below approximately 80%, then the hypothesis (and by extension the predictive approach) will be considered falsified.

cited_evidence.text: We applied atomic-resolution chemical mapping for the distribution and fluctuation of elements in high-entropy thermoelectric materials with a variety of elemental combinations. With the fluctuation evaluation of each element, we clearly revealed that the fluctuations of alloying elements were directly related to the discrepancy on atomic mass, radius, and electronegativity of these elements to the matrix elements in high-entropy samples. With the estimation on the respective contributions of the element characteristics, we found that the mass and electronegativity have the comparable contribution to local chemical fluctuation while there is a slight influence from the radius. Moreover, the local chemical fluctuation tailored by altering the constituent elements could reduce the lattice thermal conductivity, in addition to the increased entropy by combining more elements. Large lattice distortion and strain fluctuation were induced by strong elemental fluctuation to largely strengthen phonon scattering for low lattice thermal conductivity. AbstractHigh-Entropy Alloys (HEAs) are a new family of crystalline random alloys with four or more elements in a simple unit cell, at the forefront of materials research for their exceptional mechanical properties. Their strong chemical disorder leads to mass and force-constant fluctuations which are expected to strongly reduce phonon lifetime, responsible for thermal transport, similarly to glasses. Still, the long range order would associate HEAs to crystals with a complex disordered unit cell. These two families of materials, however, exhibit very different phonon dynamics, still leading to similar thermal properties. The question arises on the positioning of HEAs in this context. Here we present an exhaustive experimental investigation of the lattice dynamics in a HEA, Fe20Co20Cr20Mn20Ni20, using inelastic neutron and X-ray scattering. proposals.intervention: Develop and test a predictive machine-learning model that explicitly incorporates descriptors of chemical disorder and anharmonic lattice dynamics.
proposals.conditions: Train the model on a database of high-entropy alloys measured between 300 K and 600 K with well‐characterized equiatomic compositions; then validate against new samples prepared by standard melting and homogenization treatments.
proposals.structural_mediator: Atomic‐scale disorder and local lattice distortions
proposals.mechanism: Variations in atomic masses and force constants at the local scale enhance phonon scattering. Incorporating these descriptors allows the model to capture the strong deviation from ideal lattice behavior that leads to lower phonon thermal conductivity.
proposals.predicted_outcome: The model is expected to reduce the prediction error for phonon thermal conductivity by at least 30% compared to conventional Debye or perturbative approaches; predictions should fall within 10% of experimental values for alloys with near-ideal equiatomic disorder.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This approach provides a rationale (enhancing phonon scattering via disorder descriptors), sets a numerical improvement target (30% error reduction), limits applicability to alloys with well-characterized equiatomic disorder, and can be falsified if the model’s predictions deviate by more than 25% from measured values.

proposals.material_system: CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy with nanoscale oxide precipitates
proposals.intervention: Apply a rapid solidification or severe plastic deformation process to induce and control a dispersion of nanoscale oxide precipitates in the alloy.
proposals.conditions: Process samples to produce a range of precipitate fractions and sizes, then perform thermal conductivity measurements at room temperature; use electron microscopy to confirm precipitate dimensions and distributions.
proposals.structural_mediator: Nanoscale second-phase oxide precipitates dispersed in the disordered matrix
proposals.mechanism: Additional interfaces provided by precipitates serve as scattering centers for phonons, effectively reducing phonon mean free paths. The predictive approach would include these microstructural heterogeneities to accurately forecast thermal transport properties.
proposals.predicted_outcome: The enhanced model is expected to improve prediction accuracy by approximately 25% over methods that do not account for nanoscale features; an optimal precipitate loading is identified where the measured conductivity is significantly (e.g., >20%) lower than that in a homogeneous alloy.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: It introduces a specific processing intervention whose effect (enhanced phonon scattering due to precipitates) can be directly correlated with improved model predictions, clearly defining experimental benchmarks (precipitate density and conductivity reduction) for falsification.

proposals.material_system: CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy synthesized via conventional casting versus additive manufacturing
proposals.intervention: Conduct a comparative study between conventionally cast samples and additive manufactured samples to generate distinct microstructures with different grain sizes and residual heterogeneities.
proposals.conditions: Fabricate one set of samples using standard casting (yielding coarse grains) and another using additive manufacturing techniques (yielding refined, highly controlled microstructures) with subsequent annealing to minimize composition gradients; perform thermal conductivity tests over a temperature range of 250–700 K.
proposals.mechanism: Additional grain boundaries in the fine-grained (additively manufactured) samples increase phonon scattering, thus lowering thermal conductivity. A predictive model that accounts for these microstructural size effects should yield improved accuracy for the additively manufactured alloys.
proposals.predicted_outcome: The model should show a statistically significant improvement in correlation (e.g., >20% lower deviation from experimental measurements) for the additively manufactured alloy compared to conventional predictions for cast alloys.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This approach defines applicability limits based on processing routes, offers a clear experimental contrast, and provides a decisive benchmark (grain size-dependent thermal conductivity differences) that would falsify the hypothesis if no marked improvement is observed.

proposals.material_system: CrMnFeCoNi and related high-entropy alloys with minor elemental tuning
proposals.intervention: Perform in-situ neutron scattering experiments to measure phonon dispersion relations, focusing on detecting soft phonon modes predicted by the new predictive approach.
proposals.conditions: Carry out experiments over a wide temperature range (from 10 K to 400 K) and under controlled pressure conditions; compare experimental dispersion curves with those predicted by the model across several alloy compositions with slight elemental variations.
proposals.structural_mediator: Soft vibrational modes and localized phonon states in disordered lattices
proposals.mechanism: The hypothesis is that chemically-induced disorder leads to characteristic soft modes that dramatically enhance phonon scattering. By directly linking these modes with low thermal conductivity, the predictive approach gains a robust physical basis.
proposals.predicted_outcome: A correlation of over 80% between predicted and observed soft mode energies would support the model. Conversely, if neutron scattering fails to detect the anticipated soft modes within a 10% deviation of the predicted energy values, the hypothesis would be falsified.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This approach targets the fundamental vibrational mechanism and provides a clearly defined experimental benchmark (soft mode detection via neutron scattering) to directly confirm or refute the predictive model’s physical basis.
